hard.q: Wij hebben twee kinderen: ___ kinderen wonen nu in Brussel.
hard.e: het kind è una het-parola, ma al plurale si usa sempre onze. ons solo con una het-parola al singolare (ons kind).
hard.tt: Abbiamo due figli: i nostri figli adesso abitano a Bruxelles.

hard.q: Van wie zijn de sleutels? Van Sofie? — Ja, ze zijn van ___.
hard.e: Dopo van serve la forma oggetto: van haar (di lei). zij è soggetto, hun è "loro".
hard.tt: Di chi sono le chiavi? Di Sofie? — Sì, sono sue.

hard.q: Tom en Lies, is dat ___ auto daar?
hard.e: "Vostro" si dice jullie (non accentato anche je; in Fiandra, con gij/ge, anche uw): jullie auto, senza articolo.
hard.tt: Tom e Lies, è vostra quella macchina là?

hard.q: Mijn broer en zijn vrouw komen morgen met ___ kinderen.
hard.e: Il possessore è plurale (mio fratello e sua moglie): hun kinderen. Non hen, che è un pronome oggetto.
hard.tt: Mio fratello e sua moglie vengono domani con i loro figli.

hard.q: Come si chiama suo fratello (di lei)?
hard.e: Hoe heet (non wat) + haar broer: il possessore è lei. In Fiandre si sente anche Hoe noemt…?

hard.q: I nostri figli hanno le loro bici.
hard.e: onze (plurale) e hun (di loro). Niente articolo davanti al possessivo.

hard.q: Questo è il nostro appartamento a Gand.
hard.a: Dit is ons appartement in Gent
hard.e: het appartement è una het-parola al singolare: ons. E nessun articolo prima del possessivo.
hard.tt: Questo è il nostro appartamento a Gand.

hard.q: Prendi la tua giacca e la sua borsa (di lei)?
hard.a: Neem je je jas en haar tas
hard.e: Domanda: Neem je (verbo + soggetto), poi il possessivo je jas: due je di fila, uno soggetto e uno possessivo.
hard.tt: Prendi la tua giacca e la sua borsa?

en.note:
The idea

Possessives tell you whose something is. Good news: they work much like in English.

  • No article in front of a possessive, just as in English: "my book" is mijn boek, not het mijn boek.
  • The possessive depends on the owner, as in English: zijn moeder is his mother, haar moeder is her mother.

The table

hijzijnzijn moeder

zij (they)hunhun boeken

Ons or onze?

This is the only possessive that changes. ons in front of a singular het-word (ons huis), onze everywhere else: de-words (onze stad) and plurals (onze kinderen).

Jouw or je?

As with the pronouns, je is the unstressed, more common form: Is dat je fiets?. jouw is for emphasis: Is dat jouw fiets of mijn fiets?

"It's mine": van mij

Where English uses mine, yours, hers, Dutch uses van + object pronoun: Van wie is dat? — Het is van mij (Whose is that? — It's mine). Where English uses 's, Dutch uses van too: de fiets van Tom (Tom's bike).

Watch out: typical mistakes for English speakers

  • Using ons with a de-word: ons stad → onze stad.
  • Copying English "mine": Het is mijn. → Het is van mij.
  • Mixing up hun (their) and hen (them): hen boeken → hun boeken.
  • Remember that zijn is also the verb "to be", and haar also means "her" as an object (and "hair"!): context tells you which.
en.vlaams: In spoken Flemish, together with gij/ge, people use uw among friends too: "Is dat uw fiets?" can be completely informal.

items.say: Van wie is dat? Het is van mij.
items.q: Van wie is dat? — Het is ___.

drills.e: On its own after the verb: van mij.

g.van mij: mine (on its own, after the verb)
g.mijn: my (only in front of a noun)
g.van ik: ik is a subject: after van you need mij

hard.q: Wij hebben twee kinderen: ___ kinderen wonen nu in Brussel.
hard.e: het kind is a het-word, but in the plural it's always onze. ons only goes with a singular het-word (ons kind).
hard.tt: We have two children: our children live in Brussels now.

hard.q: Van wie zijn de sleutels? Van Sofie? — Ja, ze zijn van ___.
hard.e: After van you need the object form: van haar (hers). zij is a subject (she), hun means "their".
hard.tt: Whose keys are these? Sofie's? — Yes, they're hers.

hard.q: Tom en Lies, is dat ___ auto daar?
hard.e: "Your" for more than one person is jullie (unstressed also je; in Flanders, with gij/ge, also uw): jullie auto, with no article.
hard.tt: Tom and Lies, is that your car over there?

hard.q: Mijn broer en zijn vrouw komen morgen met ___ kinderen.
hard.e: The owners are plural (my brother and his wife): hun kinderen. Not hen, which is an object pronoun (them).
hard.tt: My brother and his wife are coming tomorrow with their children.

hard.e: Hoe heet (literally "how is called") + haar broer: the owner is her. In Flanders you'll also hear Hoe noemt…?
onze (plural) and hun (their). No article in front of the possessive.

hard.q: This is our apartment in Ghent.
hard.a: Dit is ons appartement in Gent
hard.e: het appartement is a singular het-word: ons. And no article before the possessive.
hard.tt: This is our apartment in Ghent.

hard.q: Are you taking your jacket and her bag?
hard.a: Neem je je jas en haar tas
hard.e: Question: Neem je (verb + subject), then the possessive je jas: two je's in a row, one is "you" and one is "your".
hard.tt: Are you taking your jacket and her bag?
